prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Grid Dispatcher: requirements→Wildmere; priority safety>protection>export. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss, shutdown on confirmed fire; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (isolated on fire/overheat), Nacelle Condition Monitor→Turbine Sensor Bus. Mode Turbine Lockout: no remote restart during fire investigation. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment; mode Substation Degraded; alarms not cleared merely because detector normal. Substation Operator switches only in active window with Control Engineer authorization, notifies Grid Dispatcher. Outages: Marine Coordinator vessel timing; Electrical Technician post-isolation inspection; Work Permit Portal updated first; Duty Planner records times. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry/alarms→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room keeps last validated limit on comms loss. Operations Radio Console: voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft; Vessel Master read-back; Transfer Manifest Addendum from Duty Planner. Evacuation: Personnel Tracking Console; HSE Officer advises re-entry; Field Supervisor status→Shore Control Room. North/South Access Scanners: own active credential with current area/time authorization else deny, barrier closed (incl. incomplete check); no override; south anti-tailgating; visitors/escorts verified; denial→Field Supervisor/HSE Officer; tamper-protected log of every attempt; faulty→out of service, alternative with named approver; credential-free emergency egress. East Service Lift: door-interlock/overload check before movement; Field Supervisor pre-shift inspection (hoist, suspension, cables), records results/defects in maintenance system; Electrical Technician checks supply/protective devices; capacity/instructions legible; safety defect blocks release until repaired/verified; Work Permit Portal restrictions checked; Duty Planner confirms capacity limits; boarding briefing; Personnel Tracking Console records entry/exit;

New part:
S889: The west route landing doors are inspected for damage, secure closure, and unobstructed movement.
S890: The operator confirms that the car floor is level with the boarding landing before permitting entry or exit.
S891: Lighting inside the car and at each landing must be adequate for safe movement and inspection.
S892: The operator checks that the controls respond correctly and that the emergency stop is accessible.
S893: Door interlocks and other protective devices must be functional before the lift is placed in service.
S894: Protective devices must not be bypassed to maintain access or avoid delay.
S895: The operator confirms that the expected load, including tools and carried equipment, remains within the rated capacity.
S896: Passengers distribute themselves and their equipment to avoid obstructing the doors or control panel.
S897: Loose tools and materials are secured against movement during travel.
S898: The operator confirms that all occupants are ready and that the doors are fully closed before starting movement.
S899: During travel, occupants remain inside the car and avoid interfering with the controls or doors.
S900: The operator monitors lift movement for unusual noise, vibration, hesitation, or irregular stopping.
S901: Any unexpected movement or control response requires the operator to stop the lift at the nearest safe landing when practicable.
S902: If the car stops between landings, occupants use the designated alarm or communication method and remain inside the car.
S903: Personnel do not attempt to open doors or climb out of a stopped car without direction from the response team.
S904: At the destination, the operator confirms that the car is level and stationary before opening the doors.
S905: Occupants exit without crowding, and the operator checks that tools and equipment have been removed from the car.
S906: The Field Supervisor ensures that the lift is left secure and that any irregularity is reported through the established site process.
S907: The West Service Lift is removed from service if a condition could compromise safe movement, pending assessment and corrective action.
S908: The system measures operational performance against approved service objectives and documented fleet baselines.
S909: Availability is reported for each turbine and for the fleet, with planned maintenance and forced outages classified separately.
S910: Energy production measures include delivered energy, production lost during downtime, and the duration of grid-related restrictions.
S911: Maintenance performance is assessed through work completion time, repeat work, overdue tasks, and the proportion of work completed as planned.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
